findings.detail: The validationCURRENT_WALL comment says 'after its ledger's close time' (Validations.h:50-55), but isCurrent() compares signTime against local now (Validations.h:162-165); no ledger close time enters the predicate. Any reader trusting the comment will misstate the window by the gap between signing time and ledger close time.
findings.title: The 5-minute validation window is measured from signing time vs now, not from the ledger's close time

findings.detail: No wall-clock bound exists on a peer proposal's close time (absence finding 7, 0 hits for a wall/now/bound check on closeTime in Consensus.h). A malicious validator may propose any close time; it is only rounded (T-22) and voted on (T-24). S-08 shows a +3600 s proposal entering the vote with 1 vote and losing to the honest bin.
findings.title: A peer may propose any close time; the only defence is the vote

findings.detail: No wall-clock check exists on a ledger's own close time at accept time (absence finding 8). doAccept()/buildLedger() take the consensus close time as given and apply effCloseTime() (T-23); the only ledger-level wall-clock check is canBeCurrent() on the PARENT close time within 5 minutes (T-33). A close-time mismatch with the validated ledger is logged as 'MISMATCH on close time' (LedgerHistory.cpp:384-389), i.e. treated as Byzantine evidence, not clock error.
findings.title: No wall-clock check on a ledger's own close time at accept; only the parent close time is bounded

findings.detail: ConsensusParms defines validationVALID_WALL/LOCAL/EARLY (5/3/3 min) with the same values as ValidationParms, but a tree-wide search finds zero references outside their definitions (T-34). The live parameters are the ValidationParms ones (T-05--T-07). Any pack or simulator citing ConsensusParms.h for the windows cites dead code.
findings.title: The ConsensusParms validation windows are dead copies; cite Validations.h

findings.detail: grep -rn 'ledgerMAX_CLOSE' src/ include/ docs/ returns 0 hits (T-35). The maximum-time concepts that exist are ledgerMAX_CONSENSUS = 15 s, ledgerABANDON_CONSENSUS = 120 s (T-28), and the 10-minute anomaly bound in shouldCloseLedger (T-27). Any claim citing a ledgerMAX_CLOSE value is unsourced against this tree.
findings.title: There is no ledgerMAX_CLOSE constant

findings.detail: There is no NTP/SNTP client and no consumption of the sntp_servers config (absence finding 3: only a config-section name and a doc comment), no leap-second handling (0 hits), and no DST/timezone handling on the consensus path (0 hits in clock logic). Time synchronisation is entirely external to the node; the code assumes the operator synchronises the OS clock and tolerates the rest via the windows and the median offset (T-10, T-26). S-07/S-08 model the consequences.
findings.title: No NTP, no leap-second, no DST handling: synchronisation is entirely external

findings.detail: xrpl.org says fewer than 20% faulty validators does not impede consensus (T-39, ~80% validation quorum concept), while checkConsensus declares consensus at minCONSENSUS_PCT = 67% of proposers in the round (T-28). The figures measure different things and must not be presented as the same threshold (D-02).
findings.title: 67% (round consensus) and 80% (validation quorum) are different thresholds

findings.detail: xrpl.org says close times are 'usually' rounded by 10 s (T-38), but the code default resolution is 30 s (T-20); 10 s is only the genesis resolution and the finest bin. The two reconcile through T-21: the resolution adapts down to 10 s when nodes consistently agree, so a healthy live network sits at 10 s while a fresh or disagreeing network starts at 30 s (D-03).
findings.title: 'Usually 10 s' rounding (docs) vs 30 s default (code), bridged by adaptation

findings.detail: The close offset is logged at info level ('Our close offset is estimated at ...', RCLConsensus.cpp:724-725) with no threshold, warning, or metric attached (absence finding 10). A node with a badly skewed clock is silently pulled toward the median (T-26) or silently drops others' validations as stale (T-11/T-12).
findings.title: No clock-skew alerting or operator warning exists

findings.detail: Two clocks govern validation timing: the wall-clock NetClock drives isCurrent() (T-10), while the monotonic steady_clock drives the SeqEnforcer (T-15) and the Validations expiry clocks. A signing time that jumps backwards is handled only by the +1 s floor for own validations (T-18) and by the sequence enforcer for remote ones; there is no monotonic-clock enforcement of signing times (absence finding 9).
findings.title: Validation timing runs on two clocks: wall clock for currency, steady clock for sequence enforcement

findings.detail: The UNL-expiry bow-out (T-36) compares the validator-list expiry against app_.timeKeeper().now() -- raw wall time, not the network-adjusted closeTime(). A node whose wall clock is fast can bow out while its adjusted clock is still fine, and a node whose wall clock is slow can keep validating on an expired list.
findings.title: UNL-expiry bow-out uses raw wall time, not the adjusted clock

findings.detail: Close-time votes are walked highest-time first so that, among close times tied for the most votes, the earliest wins ('The smaller value is the safer choice', Consensus.h:1606-1611). The avalanche round-count gates that apply to transaction disputes do not apply to close time: getNeededWeight is called with currentRounds = 0, minimumRounds = 0 ('We don't track rounds for close time', Consensus.h:1578) (D-04). S-06 reproduces the tie: two bins with 4 votes each, earliest (-50 s offset) adopted, no consensus.
findings.title: Close-time ties resolve to the earliest time, and dispute round gates do not apply to close time

pack: Timestamp Validation and Clock-Skew Tolerance in postfiatd
